# Vercel Usage restyle

Only Usage content and its own portaled surfaces receive the supplied dark
palette in both light and dark modes. Shared header, navigation, header logo,
footer, help, Purple, and other routes keep their existing styles.

Existing text sizes, spacing, gauge dimensions (112px with 9px strokes), icon
tile size (60px), and bar height (8px) are retained per the implementation plan.
The supplied typography weights, letter spacing and corner values are applied;
the supplied larger typography/component sizes are deliberately not substituted.

## Files changed by this task

- `src/components/usage/usage.module.css`: local palette, type, corners, states,
  controls, progress, icon tile, price pill, menu and tooltip surface styles.
- `src/components/usage/PlanCard.tsx`: Usage surface classes, Premium sparkle
  variant (Purple retains Zap), and local error presentation.
- `src/components/usage/AllowanceGauge.tsx`: solid ring paint override; Purple
  retains its gradient.
- `src/components/ui/Tooltip.tsx`: optional bubble `className`; unchanged default.
- `public/fonts/inter/InterVariable.woff2`: bundled Inter variable font.
- `public/fonts/inter/OFL.txt`: Inter's SIL Open Font License.
- `tests/browser/app.spec.ts`: Usage matrix, allowance states, controls, contrast,
  palette isolation, and screenshots.
- `design/usage/README.md` and `design/usage/screenshots/`: delivery record.

The working tree already contained other edits, including edits in several of
these files; those remain intact. Nothing is committed or pushed.

Existing utilities and shared tooltip styles use aliases defined **on Usage or
its surfaces only**: `--background`, `--card`, `--surface`, `--foreground`,
`--body`, `--muted-foreground`, `--border`, `--border-hover`, `--control-border`,
`--link`, `--ring`, `--accent`, `--appearance-focus`, `--appearance-link`,
`--appearance-wash`, `--appearance-border`, `--appearance-card`,
`--appearance-decoration`, `--appearance-shadow`, `--appearance-focus-shadow`,
`--appearance-radius`, `--appearance-control-radius`, `--appearance-badge-radius`,
`--plan-pink`, `--font-plus-jakarta`, `--tooltip-green`, `--tooltip-yellow`,
`--tooltip-pink`. `--button-hover-filter: none` is set on Usage controls only.

JetBrains Mono remains the existing locally loaded label font, with 500 weight
and 0.2em tracking. Inter is only requested when Vercel Usage uses it.

## Verification

Run against a disposable local Docker PostgreSQL database; Next.js runs on host:

```sh
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npx vitest run tests/usage-allowance-state.test.ts tests/appearance.test.ts
npx tsx scripts/test-usage-db.ts --e2e-only '--browser=app.spec.ts,feature-gates.spec.ts,--grep,Usage local restyle|Vercel information controls|Usage link supports|Vercel allowance states|Usage handles monthly'
```

The Usage matrix covers Purple and Vercel, light and dark, desktop and mobile.
Vercel checks include healthy/low/empty/reserved daily and monthly allowances,
sent/queued legends, disabled checkout, Premium management, billing warning and
error states, keyboard menus/tooltips, focus, hover, overflow, and automated axe
checks (including contrast). Rendered Usage CSS is checked for blue and gradients,
visible text for emoji, and navigation away for token leakage.

Purple screenshots were compared to pre-change captures: matching pixels within
a one-level channel antialiasing tolerance, excluding the variable Next.js dev
indicator. Screenshots are saved alongside this record.

Final results: typecheck and lint passed; 16 unit tests passed; 20 targeted
browser tests passed, including all automated axe checks. `git diff --check`
passed. Database fixtures were disposable and cleaned up after each run.
